svg.title: Compare Contribution per Paid Service Hour
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-sub-niche-contribution-per-paid-hour; chart type: horizontal_bars; title: Compare Contribution per Paid Service Hour; subtitle: Five illustrative sub-niche bids after direct delivery costs, before shared overhead.; chapter number: 2; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: All values are USD contribution per paid service hour, not net margin percentages or published market rates. Revenue equivalent equals contract revenue divided by all attributable paid service hours. Direct cost includes loaded field labor, routine consumables, and service-specific equipment. Shared supervision, sales, administration, and owner net remain outside these bars.; caption: Rank measured account economics rather than building labels. Extra dwell time, access delays, overtime, and rework can erase a nominal medical or industrial price premium.; stages: label: Outpatient medical offices; value: $14 contribution from $52 revenue less $38 direct cost; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Model label contact times, isolation-area restrictions, PPE, and exposure-related training in paid hours. Do not price regulated waste handling into an ordinary janitorial scope without the required operating capability.; label: Light industrial offices; value: $12 contribution from $48 revenue less $36 direct cost; numeric value: 12.0; detail: Limit the modeled scope to offices and agreed common areas. Separately quote production-floor work, machinery proximity, unusual soils, and site-specific safety training.; label: Professional office suites; value: $11 contribution from $44 revenue less $33 direct cost; numeric value: 11.0; detail: Cluster nearby suites to reduce paid travel. Measure desk density, restroom fixtures, alarm procedures, elevator delays, and tenant-requested extras rather than bidding from square footage alone.; label: Multitenant common areas; value: $11 contribution from $46 revenue less $35 direct cost; numeric value: 11.0; detail: Specify lobby appearance standards, restroom replenishment, public access windows, and weekend attendance. Separate tenant-private cleaning from property-manager common-area obligations to prevent unpaid scope expansion.; label: Private education facilities; value: $8 contribution from $40 revenue less $32 direct cost; numeric value: 8.0; detail: Price restroom intensity, event resets, safeguarding-related access procedures, and academic calendar changes. Quote summer floor restoration separately and confirm whether monthly billing continues through closures.

text.title: Compare Contribution per Paid Service Hour
text.tspan: Compare Contribution per Paid Service Hour

rect.title: label: Outpatient medical offices; value: $14 contribution from $52 revenue less $38 direct cost; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Model label contact times, isolation-area restrictions, PPE, and exposure-related training in paid hours. Do not price regulated waste handling into an ordinary janitorial scope without the required operating capability.

label: Light industrial offices; value: $12 contribution from $48 revenue less $36 direct cost; numeric value: 12.0; detail: Limit the modeled scope to offices and agreed common areas. Separately quote production-floor work, machinery proximity, unusual soils, and site-specific safety training.

label: Professional office suites; value: $11 contribution from $44 revenue less $33 direct cost; numeric value: 11.0; detail: Cluster nearby suites to reduce paid travel. Measure desk density, restroom fixtures, alarm procedures, elevator delays, and tenant-requested extras rather than bidding from square footage alone.

label: Multitenant common areas; value: $11 contribution from $46 revenue less $35 direct cost; numeric value: 11.0; detail: Specify lobby appearance standards, restroom replenishment, public access windows, and weekend attendance. Separate tenant-private cleaning from property-manager common-area obligations to prevent unpaid scope expansion.

label: Private education facilities; value: $8 contribution from $40 revenue less $32 direct cost; numeric value: 8.0; detail: Price restroom intensity, event resets, safeguarding-related access procedures, and academic calendar changes. Quote summer floor restoration separately and confirm whether monthly billing continues through closures.

text.title: Assumptions: All values are USD contribution per paid service hour, not net margin percentages or published market rates. Revenue equivalent equals contract revenue divided by all attributable paid service hours. Direct cost includes loaded field labor, routine consumables, and service-specific equipment. Shared supervision, sales, administration, and owner net remain outside these bars.
